property_summary: For any caller, if Collect(...) is called when the holder has enough balance (>= MinSum and >= amount) and unlockTime passed, the reference always forwards the ether and returns success (so Collect does not revert and c.Acc(caller).balance is decreased by amount and address(c).balance decreased accordingly); replacing call with send can fail when the recipient's fallback uses more than 2300 gas, causing Collect to revert or behave differently — so the mutant can fail for some adversarial recipient contract.

For any depositor who has >= MinSum and whose unlockTime has passed, calling Collect(am) always succeeds (does not revert) and reduces their recorded balance by am in the reference; replacing call with send can cause the external transfer to fail (due to limited gas) and thus make Collect revert or not reduce balance, breaking this rule for some adversarial recipient.

For any depositor who has balance >= MinSum and unlockTime passed, calling Collect(amount) always succeeds (does not revert) and reduces the contract's recorded balance by amount in the reference; changing call to send can make the external transfer fail for an adversarial recipient and thus cause Collect to revert or not reduce the recorded balance.

For any depositor with sufficient recorded balance and expired unlockTime, calling Collect(amount) always succeeds (does not revert) and reduces the depositor's recorded balance by amount in the reference; changing the external transfer from call to send can fail against a malicious recipient (whose fallback consumes >2300 gas), causing Collect to revert and thus violate this property for some inputs.

For any depositor with balance >= MinSum and unlockTime in the past, calling Collect(amount) always succeeds (does not revert) and reduces the depositor's recorded balance by amount on the reference; changing the value transfer from call to send can cause the external transfer to fail for a malicious recipient (whose fallback uses >2300 gas) and thus make Collect revert — violating the rule for some inputs.
After Collect reverts (failed external transfer), the caller's Acc balance decreases (on P) — i.e., Collect either reverts or reduces caller balance by _am.
If Collect reverts then the caller did not meet the preconditions (so for any call with acc.balance>=MinSum and acc.balance>=_am and block.timestamp>acc.unlockTime, Collect must not revert).
If Collect is called when the caller meets the withdrawal conditions, the call must not revert (i.e., it succeeds) for all input amounts and times.
If caller has at least MinSum and at least _am and time > unlockTime, then Collect must not revert (i.e., succeeds) and thus reverted == false.
If calling Collect does not revert for a caller who meets withdrawal conditions, then the call must succeed (i.e., reverted == false).
